create.title: Physical return and fixed-y character-Abel bound for the R1 residue
create.statement_tex: On lines a,b>0 with a/2+b<1/4, the physical symmetric-profile limit of R^ar[R_1] equals int_0^N y^(-3/4){e(sqrt(X max(1,y)))-e(sqrt(XN))} sum_j sum_q chi_4(q)q^(-1)V_j^*(2sqrt(Xy)/(D_jq))phi(y/((H_j+1)q))dy. For Q_j(y)=sqrt(Xy)/D_j, the fixed-(j,y) q-amplitude has sup norm plus sampled variation <<_W Q_j(y)^(-1), hence character Abel gives <<_W D_j/sqrt(Xy). Nonempty support forces D_j<=4sqrt(Xy), the y and geometric scale sums are O_W(1), and the restored physical contribution is O_W(X^(1/4)). This begins only after the accepted physical profile limits.
create.next_action: Use only for the accepted physical profile limit; retain finite-height contour tails outside this lemma.

update.reason_for_promotion: Three independent Round-24 derivations agree on the exact physical y-return, admissible conditional character-series order, fixed-y sampled BV, period-four Abel bound, y/scale summation, endpoint seams, and restored physical normalization.
update.statement_tex: After the accepted symmetric physical-profile limits, the recombined R_1 arithmetic residue has the exact y-integral return recorded in M9-M1-R1-physical-return-character-Abel and is O_W(1) on the normalized M1 scale. Restoring the external active-M1 factor gives O_W(X^(1/4)). The result retains all actual scales, H_j+1 floors, the one-sided top half-star, height endpoint zero, and the lower-minus-upper radial phase; it is not a uniform arbitrary-finite-top-height statement.
update.next_action: Treat the recombined physical R_1 residue as target-safe and keep the two diagonal transition traces separate.

update.reason_for_promotion: The finite Cauchy reduction, both physical endpoint-prefix bounds, artificial-pole cancellation, and the recombined physical R_1 arithmetic-residue bound are now all proved with compatible normalizations and residue ledger.
update.statement_tex: For M=1, the explicit radial endpoint boundary package is target-safe after the accepted physical profile limits. Finite Cauchy algebra returns it to the lower and upper original-sector prefixes plus the recombined R_1 arithmetic residue after the artificial-pole cancellation; the lower prefix is O(X^(1/4)log X), the upper prefix is O_W(X^(1/4)), and R^ar[R_1] is O_W(X^(1/4)) physically. This node does not include the two separate diagonal transition traces.
update.next_action: Use the closed endpoint package when attacking the two remaining diagonal transition traces; do not infer arbitrary finite-top-height uniformity.

update.statement_tex: The renormalized radial sides are removed and the entire physical endpoint/residue package is target-safe. The only unresolved parts of this operator are the two diagonal single-transition traces and their outside-height limits.
update.next_action: Freeze the exact pair of diagonal transition traces and test whether their vector-Hilbert structure gives a target-sized bound after the endpoint package is removed.

update.statement_tex: In diagonal heights alpha=Im s+Im(u+v)/2 and beta=Im s-Im(u+v)/2, the renormalized radial sides, both physical endpoint prefixes, and the recombined R_1 arithmetic residue are target-safe. Prove a target-sized bound for the two remaining exact single-transition traces together with their outside-height limits and any separately retained axial residues.
update.next_action: Derive a common finite formula for the positive and negative diagonal transition traces after subtracting every accepted endpoint/residue term, then seek a vector-Hilbert or signed character-Abel estimate.

reject.reason: Before the physical top-profile limit, the finite inverse Mellin profile has noncompact logarithmic tails and the compact-support sampled-BV lemma does not apply uniformly.
Without bounded partial sums of chi_4, a q-asymp-Q block has Q terms of size Q^(-1), losing the inverse-support-length gain and retaining normalized N_X^(1/4)-type capacity.
